title: Protocol-Based Plugin Architecture for Data Ingestion
business: Data engineering teams building modular ingestion pipelines that must support diverse, third-party data sources without tight coupling.
problem: Runtime errors occur when ingestion modules expect specific attributes from dynamic data objects, leading to attribute errors during production execution.
solution: Mypy Protocols enable structural subtyping, allowing developers to define an interface based on required attributes rather than inheritance, while type narrowing safely confirms object capabilities at runtime.
steps: Define a Protocol class specifying the required methods or attributes for a data source.
Annotate ingestion functions to accept the Protocol type instead of concrete classes.
Implement type narrowing using isinstance() or type guards to verify object structure before access.
Run mypy to statically validate that all passed objects satisfy the Protocol requirements.
outcome: Increased system reliability through compile-time detection of missing interface implementations, reducing runtime attribute errors.
limitation: Protocols rely on structural compatibility, which can lead to false positives if two objects share the same attribute names but have different semantic meanings; verify with runtime checks.

questions.question: In Protocol-Based Plugin Architecture for Data Ingestion, how does the solution address runtime attribute errors?
options: By enforcing strict inheritance hierarchies for all data sources.
By using Mypy Protocols to define required attributes and validating them statically.
By converting all dynamic data into JSON strings before processing.
By disabling dynamic typing entirely across the codebase.
questions.explanation: The solution leverages Protocols to define structural requirements, allowing Mypy to catch missing attributes before the code runs.
questions.evidence: Mypy Protocols enable structural subtyping, allowing developers to define an interface based on required attributes rather than inheritance, while type narrowing safely confirms object capabilities at runtime.

questions.question: What is a primary limitation of the approach described in Protocol-Based Plugin Architecture for Data Ingestion?
options: Protocols cannot be used with third-party libraries.
Structural compatibility might ignore semantic differences between objects with identical attribute names.
Mypy cannot perform type narrowing on objects that implement Protocols.
The approach requires all objects to inherit from a common base class.
questions.explanation: Because Protocols check structure (names of attributes) rather than intent, objects that happen to have the same names but different behaviors can pass checks incorrectly.
questions.evidence: Protocols rely on structural compatibility, which can lead to false positives if two objects share the same attribute names but have different semantic meanings; verify with runtime checks.
